correctness.rationale: Correctness was checked by reconstructing the full chain: uniform point in doubled cube -> iid U(0,1) coordinate coverage probabilities -> Gamma(d,1); maxima of exponential samples give exact mean as P(Gamma<=M_m). Gamma density Stirling expansion contributes (1-s^2)/3; E[M_m]-log m contributes Euler gamma. Each translated cube changes the normalized union by at most 2^-d, so McDiarmid yields 2 exp(-2t^2 4^d/m). At m~exp(d+O(sqrt d)), choose t proportional to d^-1/2; the tails are summable. The two-sided threshold inversion via monotonicity proves the a.s. constant-order logarithmic quantile law. Python standard-library verifier passed 120 deterministic cases including exact rational finite formula checks and numerical second-term diagnostics. Simulations are only diagnostics, not proof.

originality.rationale: The exact random-cube expected coverage is demonstrably prior in Zhigljavsky and Noonan (2020), Section 4.2. The claim evaluated here is instead the almost-sure, all-fixed-alpha threshold in dimension with a sharp additive constant in logarithmic sample size, including a joint gamma Edgeworth/Gumbel correction and exponentially strong self-averaging. This is not asserted or proved by the inspected prior Section 4.2, by the 2026 union-of-translates paper, or by the closest published mathematical-record searches. Targeted source and alias searches disclosed no stated covering theorem, although historical priority remains at risk because the derivation applies standard probability tools to an exact known mean.
residual_risks: The exact finite mean formula is substantially covered by Zhigljavsky–Noonan (2020); only the new a.s. threshold and explicit constant are claimed.
As a consequence of known finite coverage and standard probabilistic tools, an equivalent high-dimensional almost-sure threshold might exist in older, unindexed random-coverage literature.
Only abstract-level material was accessible for Penrose (2023) and the random-polytope comparison; no negative full-document assessment is asserted for them.
Semantic searches of published mathematical abstracts are incomplete and cannot certify uniqueness.

value.rationale: In high dimension each of exponentially many congruent cube translations covers an exponentially small fraction of their doubled support; determining the sample count for any fixed macroscopic partial-coverage target is a natural geometric probability question. The theorem finds the exact exponential base e, the sqrt(d) Gaussian window, and, nontrivially, the constant *multiplicative sample-size factor* at every target fraction. Half-volume coverage occurs at e^(-gamma-1/3)e^d almost surely. The same hitting-time constant governs realized configurations, not merely an expectation. This is a precise benchmark beyond a known exact mean; it is not a named constant for an arbitrary unmotivated slice.
